_readme: Sec 1 G3 E21CC dashboard, copied unchanged from the HOD's file 'E21CC Dashboard Template (Sec 1 G3 MTL).html' (5 Nov 2026). Rendered by vE21d in index.html. Edit here, then run tools/enrich.py.

CAIT 3: Understands how similarities and differences between contexts affect their perspective or approach.
CAIT 4: Adjusts their approach using different perspectives and strategies, applying learning in unfamiliar contexts.
CCI 1: Conveys and evaluates knowledge to co-construct ideas, considering purpose and context.
CCI 2: Responds with respect and empathy, sensitive to diverse backgrounds.
CCI 3: Manages disagreements, takes in suggestions and contributes to shared goals.
CCI 4: Determines and assumes their role by considering group dynamics.
CGC 1: Describes and explains issues affecting Singapore, understanding multiple perspectives.
CGC 2: Plans and organises programmes with others, with support; differentiates civic roles.

st.q: “I adapt to different situations and adopt a growth mindset.”
“I communicate with empathy, collaborate effectively and lead by serving others.”
“I act with courage and integrity to make a positive change.”

year.h1: How the year develops E21CC and realises our DSOs
year.sub: Each cell names the task that maps to the milestone.

aa.label: Authentic Assessment
aa.eyebrow: SEC 1 G3 MOTHER TONGUE LANGUAGES · AUTHENTIC ASSESSMENT
aa.h1: How our authentic assessments develop E21CC and realise our DSOs

terms.1: Unit 1: New classmates, new experiences · Unit 2: Reunion · Compositions 1–2 · Listening and speaking · WA1
terms.2: Unit 3: Meet in Singapore · Emails 1–2 · Oral · WA2
terms.3: AA · Unit 4: The power of habit · Unit 5: Innovation and change · Unit 6: Ordinary people, big contributions · Composition 3 · Email 3

1.t: Unit 2: Comparing Eastern and Western New Year customs
1.y: Students compare how Eastern and Western cultures mark the New Year.

2.t: Unit 3: Comparing tourist route maps
2.y: Groups compare two local tourist route maps on choice of sites, theme, audience and presentation, then share what they find.

3.t: Unit 5: Comparing two competition posters
3.y: Students find the similarities and differences between two competition posters.

2.t: Unit 3: Designing a three-day itinerary for a foreign friend
2.y: Students design an itinerary to suit a foreign friend’s needs, using what they have learnt about Singapore.

3.t: Unit 5: Weighing views on changing animal genes
3.y: Students weigh views for and against, give their own, record it on SLS and comment on each other’s.

3.t: Unit 5: Inventing a product for an everyday problem
3.y: Groups conceive a product that solves an everyday problem, write a plan and present it.

1.t: Composition 1: Describing a character
1.y: Students convey a character through description.

1.t: Listening and speaking: Views on keeping traditional customs
1.y: Students give a view on whether traditional customs should be kept.

1.t: Composition 2: Narrative around a theme
1.y: Students organise a narrative around a theme.

2.t: Unit 3: Emails 1–2 to a named reader
2.y: Students write to a named reader for a stated purpose. The CPDD guide names CCI 1.3 as a goal of Unit 3.

2.t: Oral practice: Sharing experiences, giving suggestions
2.y: Students share experiences and give suggestions in conversation.

2.t: Oral exam Q2: Suggesting how parents can build teens’ sleep habits
2.y: After a video on sleep habits, students suggest how parents can help teens build good habits, and say how this helps.

2.t: WA2: Email paper
2.y: The email paper assesses writing for a reader and purpose.

3.t: Interview video: Student leader role
3.y: Students script and record a mock interview for a student leader role, using PEEL, and say how they would help teachers and classmates.

3.t: Email 3: Sharing an experience and a view
3.y: Students share an experience and give a view.

3.t: Email 4: Practice under exam conditions
3.y: Students practise email writing under exam conditions.

4.t: End-of-year email: Reply to a friend
4.y: Students reply to a friend for a set purpose, choosing 1 of 2: using a learning device in class, or thanking class committee members.

4.t: End-of-year composition: Narrative on a change of view
4.y: Students organise a narrative of at least 250 words around a change of view, and convey their feelings.

4.t: End-of-year comprehension: Giving a view, with an example
4.y: Students read for meaning, then say whether they agree with a stated view and back it with a real-life example.

1.t: Listening and speaking: Responding to views on customs
1.y: Students respond to classmates’ views on traditional customs.

2.t: Conversation: Taking another person’s position
2.y: Students take another person’s position in conversation.

2.t: Oral exam Q1: Imagining how the girl in the video feels
2.y: Students imagine being the girl in the video, and say how she feels and why.

3.t: Unit 6: Role-playing unsung heroes
3.y: Students appreciate the work of people who are often overlooked, and role-play them.

4.t: End-of-year composition: How an event changed their view of someone
4.y: Students tell how an event changed their view of a classmate they disliked, or of parents they thought did not understand them. They choose 1 of 2.

4.t: End-of-year email, option 2: Thanking class committee members
4.y: Students say how they would thank and support class committee members who quietly help others. Not all students choose this option.

1.t: Unit 2: Comparing views on reunion dinner as a group
1.y: Groups compare the views each member collected, sum them up and make a slide deck.

3.t: Unit 5: Agreeing on and presenting a product plan as a group
3.y: Groups discuss and agree on one product, then complete and present a plan together.

1.t: Unit 2: Why people differ on going home for reunion dinner
1.y: Students use news reports to learn why people differ on whether one must go home for reunion dinner.

2.t: Unit 3: Singapore’s places, food and cultures
2.y: Students learn about Singapore’s places, food and cultures. The CPDD guide names CGC 1.3 as a goal of Unit 3.

3.t: Unit 6: Local workers’ contribution; fact and opinion in the news
3.y: Students examine the contribution of local workers and separate fact from opinion in a Singapore news report.

3.t: Email 3: Writing about unsung heroes
3.y: Students write about unsung heroes such as the school attendant.

terms.1: Unit 1: Need or want · Unit 2: We must be sensitive · Unit 3: Overcoming challenge
terms.2: Unit 4: Inspiration · Unit 5: Courtesy · Oral exam
terms.3: AA · Unit 6: Come and eat · Unit 7: Facing challenges · Unit 8: Giving back

2.t: Unit 5: How we talk and act with different groups
2.y: Students compare how they talk and act with different groups, and give reasons.

3.t: Oral presentation: Favourite food, traditional or fusion
3.y: Students link a favourite dish to its traditional or fusion form.

1.t: Unit 3: Weighing the best step in a challenge
1.y: Students weigh the steps open to them in a challenge and identify the best one.

3.t: Unit 7: Explaining a decision in a Fishbowl discussion
3.y: In a Fishbowl on scenario cards, students explain a decision and their reasons, weighing its pros and cons.

1.t: Unit 1: Analysing a dilemma and justifying actions
1.y: Groups analyse a dilemma on a whiteboard, then present and justify possible actions.

1.t: Unit 2: Writing a motivational message to a character
1.y: Students write a motivational message to a character, with suitable words and register.

1.t: Unit 3: Writing a message of advice
1.y: Students write a message of advice and check it against a checklist.

2.t: Unit 4: Explaining song choices to the class
2.y: Students explain their song choices and present the group’s discussion to the class.

2.t: Oral exam: Sharing an experience of bringing own bags when shopping
2.y: After a video on reducing plastic, students tell of bringing their own bag or container when shopping, say how it felt, and share what they know about recycling.

3.t: Oral presentation: My favourite food, using 4P
3.y: Students organise a script with 4P, then present it to an audience.

3.t: Unit 6: Group debate on food culture
3.y: In a group debate, students sum up both sides and give a view based on evidence.

3.t: Unit 8: Presenting an infographic
3.y: Students present an infographic clearly and with confidence.

4.t: End-of-year response: Forum reply on choosing songs
4.y: Students reply on a student forum, advising how to choose songs for morning assembly and giving reasons.

4.t: End-of-year essay: Describing an experience or telling a story
4.y: Students write at least 240 words, describing an experience or telling a story.
Students read for meaning and answer open-ended questions, such as how people’s attitudes to reuse differ.

1.t: Unit 2: Telling teasing from mockery on social media
1.y: Students read a character’s feelings and tell teasing from mockery in social media posts.

1.t: Unit 2: Words of support for a friend who is hurting
1.y: Students use words of support and hope for a friend who is hurting.

2.t: Unit 4: Respecting different choices of music
2.y: Students discuss why it matters to respect each person’s different choice of music.

2.t: Unit 5: Why polite, indirect wording matters
2.y: Students discuss why indirect, polite wording protects courtesy.

2.t: Unit 5: How polite and impolite posts affect relationships
2.y: Students examine how polite and impolite posts affect relationships and image.

3.t: Unit 8: Sincerity and appreciation in giving and receiving
3.y: Students discuss sincerity, appreciation and taking advantage in giving and receiving.

2.t: Unit 4: Reworking and performing a song as a group
2.y: Groups rework the song ‘Orang Singapura’ and agree how to perform it. Students also take peer feedback on their story drafts.

1.t: Unit 2: Social media problems in the news
1.y: Students research news on common social media problems and discuss ways to address them.

2.t: Unit 4: Current issues on songs and youth
2.y: Students discuss current issues on songs and youth, and traditional songs and students.

3.t: Unit 6: Debating whether innovation keeps Malay food relevant
3.y: Students gather public comments, then debate whether innovation keeps Malay food relevant.

3.t: Unit 8: Forms of contribution in Singapore society
3.y: Students identify forms of contribution in Singapore society and discuss community work through social media.

3.t: Unit 8: Comparing forms of contribution
3.y: Students compare the many forms contribution can take.

terms.1: 1A Modules: New beginnings · Harvest festival · Tamil and me
terms.2: 1A Module: Goals · 1B Module: Keeping healthy · Oral exam
terms.3: AA · 1B Modules: The Internet · Water management

1.t: Tamil and me: How written and spoken Tamil differ
1.y: Students discuss how words change between written and spoken Tamil, then rework a dialogue for speech.

3.t: Water management: Comparing ancient Tamil and Singapore water plans
3.y: Students compare water management plans of the ancient Tamils with Singapore’s water-saving plans, and say what the ancient plans teach us.

2.t: Goals: Deciding what to do in everyday situations
2.y: Students work through situations such as a schoolmate short of money for food, and think through how to solve the problem. The guide tags responsible decision-making.

1.t: New beginnings: Recording views on a CCA
1.y: Students record their views in spoken Tamil, using words that suit the situation.

1.t: Harvest festival: Designing and presenting a brochure
1.y: Students design and present a brochure for a given situation.

1.t: Tamil and me: Exchanging views orally
1.y: Students exchange views orally in response to set questions.

2.t: Goals: Email to a friend on thoughts and feelings
2.y: Students express thoughts and feelings in a fitting style.

2.t: Oral exam: Giving and justifying views on sport and health
2.y: After a video on sports, students say which they would like to play and why, then say whether they agree that sport benefits body and mind.

3.t: Oral presentation: The CCA I like, recorded with slides
3.y: Students build slides with examples, then record their presentation.

3.t: The Internet: Making a poster on Internet use
3.y: Students gather information and make a poster on Internet use.

3.t: Water management: Writing an event article
3.y: Students write an article that suits a given situation.

4.t: End-of-year email: Reply to a friend
4.y: Students reply to a friend for a set purpose, sharing useful holiday activities or advising on healthy living. They choose 1 of 2.

4.t: End-of-year essay: An incident and the lesson learnt
4.y: Students write at least 180 words, such as on an unexpected incident and the lesson learnt.

4.t: End-of-year comprehension: Explaining ideas in own words
4.y: Students read for meaning and explain in their own words, such as why thrift matters.

1.t: Harvest festival: Conversation on Pongal
1.y: Students keep a conversation going by explaining and asking questions. The guide tags cross-cultural understanding.

2.t: Goals: Expressing ideas to suit different situations
2.y: Students express ideas and feelings to suit different situations. The guide tags social awareness.

2.t: Oral exam: Encouraging a friend to take up sport
2.y: Students say how they would encourage a friend who has no interest in sport.

4.t: End-of-year email, option 2: Advising a friend on health
4.y: Students write to a close friend whose health is suffering, advising on healthy living. Not all students choose this option.

3.t: Water management: Building on other groups’ ideas at learning corners
3.y: Groups discuss a question and write their ideas at a learning corner, then move on, read what others wrote and add their own, before returning to sum up.

1.t: Harvest festival: Pongal and cultural understanding
1.y: Students watch a video on Pongal and talk about the festival. The guide tags civic literacy, global awareness and cross-cultural understanding.

1.t: Tamil and me: The role of Tamils in Singapore
1.y: Students discuss how Tamils helped Singapore progress, then watch a video on their role, Tamil as one of four official languages, and Tamil place names.

3.t: Water management: Discussing water saving
3.y: Students watch a video and discuss water saving in class. The guide tags civic literacy and global awareness.

3.t: Water management: Water rationing and water saving in Singapore
3.y: Groups discuss whether Singapore uses water rationing and why, and what Singapore does to save water.

3.t: Water management: Singapore’s reservoirs, plants and NEWater
3.y: Students discuss how Singapore meets its water needs through reservoirs, treatment plants and NEWater.

3.t: Water management: How countries manage water
3.y: Students read how different countries manage water and answer questions. The guide tags civic literacy and global awareness.

CL.label: Chinese (CL)
CL.title: Interview 101: student leader interview
CL.format: Recorded interview video, about 3 minutes, with a written draft. Individual.
CL.when: Term 3, W2 to W6. Submitted 4 Aug 2026.
CL.builds: Builds on Term 2 oral practice: sharing experiences and giving suggestions.

CCI 1.t: Make a PEEL case for the role, with real examples
CCI 1.y: The rubric rewards clear organisation, PEEL and concrete examples. It is framed as a real interview, so purpose and context are clear. One way only: students do not build ideas with others.

CCI 1.t: Show understanding of a student leader’s duties
CCI 1.y: The top band asks for understanding of the duties of a student leader, and the draft asks how students would help teachers and classmates.

ML.label: Malay (ML)
ML.title: Makanan Kegemaran: my favourite food
ML.format: Oral presentation, 2 minutes, with a written script. Individual.
ML.builds: Builds on Unit 6: Come and eat (the food unit in the CPDD sample scheme).

CAIT 3.t: Link the dish to its traditional or fusion form
CAIT 3.y: The prompt asks what fusion dish could be created from a traditional one, or which tradition lies behind a fusion dish. No rubric line rewards this.

CCI 1.t: Organise and present the story with 4P
CCI 1.y: Students organise experience, feeling, opinion and lesson into a script, then present to an audience. The rubric rewards well-developed ideas with examples. One way only.

TL.label: Tamil (TL)
TL.title: The CCA I Like
TL.format: Recorded slide presentation, 4–5 slides, 2–3 minutes, uploaded to SLS. Individual.
TL.builds: Builds on the “The CCA I like” recording in 1A Module 1 (activity 1.4).

CCI 1.t: Explain a CCA clearly, with examples, on slides
CCI 1.y: The rubric rewards clear, connected ideas with examples, fitting images and engaged delivery. The prompts are descriptive (what, why, benefits, an experience) and one way only.
